title: Rigveda 6.70: To Heaven and earth
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.70: To Heaven and earth: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.70 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Heaven and earth. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 487v-488v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.70.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 488r
translation.original_text:
1ghṛ̱tava̍tī̱ bhuva̍nānām abhi̱śriyo̱rvī pṛ̱thvī ma̍dhu̱dughe̍ su̱peśa̍sā | dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī varu̍ṇasya̱ dharma̍ṇā̱ viṣka̍bhite a̱jare̱ bhūri̍retasā ||
2asa̍ścantī̱ bhūri̍dhāre̱ paya̍svatī ghṛ̱taṁ du̍hāte su̱kṛte̱ śuci̍vrate | rāja̍ntī a̱sya bhuva̍nasya rodasī a̱sme reta̍ḥ siñcata̱ṁ yan manu̍rhitam ||
3yo vā̍m ṛ̱jave̱ krama̍ṇāya rodasī̱ marto̍ da̱dāśa̍ dhiṣaṇe̱ sa sā̍dhati | pra pra̱jābhi̍r jāyate̱ dharma̍ṇa̱s pari̍ yu̱voḥ si̱ktā viṣu̍rūpāṇi̱ savra̍tā ||
4ghṛ̱tena̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̱bhīvṛ̍te ghṛta̱śriyā̍ ghṛta̱pṛcā̍ ghṛtā̱vṛdhā̍ | u̱rvī pṛ̱thvī ho̍tṛ̱vūrye̍ pu̱rohi̍te̱ te id viprā̍ īḻate su̱mnam i̱ṣṭaye̍ ||
translation.text:
1FILLED full of fatness, compassing all things that be, wide, spacious, dropping meath, beautiful in their form, The Heaven and the Earth by Varuṇa's decree, unwasting, rich in germs, stand parted each from each.
2The Everlasting Pair, with full streams, rich in milk, in their pure rule pour fatness for the pious man. Ye who are Regents of this world, O Earth and Heaven, pour into us the genial flow that prospers meit.
3Whoso, for righteous life, pours offerings to you, O Heaven and Earth, ye Hemispheres, that man succeeds. He in his seed is born again and spreads by Law: from you flow things diverse in form, but ruled alike.
4Enclosed in fatness, Heaven and Earth are bright therewith: they mingle with the fatness which they still increase. Wide, broad, set foremost at election of the priest, to them the singers pray for bliss to further them.

translation.original_ref: RV 6.70.5-6 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 488v
translation.original_text:
5madhu̍ no̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī mi̍mikṣatām madhu̱ścutā̍ madhu̱dughe̱ madhu̍vrate | dadhā̍ne ya̱jñaṁ dravi̍ṇaṁ ca de̱vatā̱ mahi̱ śravo̱ vāja̍m a̱sme su̱vīrya̍m ||
6ūrja̍ṁ no̱ dyauś ca̍ pṛthi̱vī ca̍ pinvatām pi̱tā mā̱tā vi̍śva̱vidā̍ su̱daṁsa̍sā | sa̱ṁra̱rā̱ṇe roda̍sī vi̱śvaśa̍mbhuvā sa̱niṁ vāja̍ṁ ra̱yim a̱sme sam i̍nvatām ||
translation.text:
5May Heaven and Earth pour down the balmy rain for us, balm-dropping, yielding balm, with balm upon your path, Bestowing by your Godhead sacrifice and wealth, great fame and strength for us and good heroic might.
6May Heaven and Earth make food swell plenteously for us, all-knowing Father, Mother, wondrous in their works. Pouring out bounties, may, in union, both the Worlds, all beneficial, send us gain, and power, and wealth.
